title: Anti-Inflammatory Effect of Ginsenoside Rg1 on LPS-Induced Septic Encephalopathy and Associated Mechanism.
authors: Chen, Yuan; Chi, Miaomiao; Qiao, Xinyu; Wang, Jiabing; Jin, Yong
one_liner_zh: 研究人参皂苷Rg1对脓毒症脑病的抗炎作用机制，涉及NF-κB和MAPK信号通路，与蛋白质-DNA互作及AI/物理模拟方法完全无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sepsis frequently occurs in patients after infection and is highly associated with death. Septic encephalopathy is characterized by dysfunction of the central nervous system, of which the root cause is a systemic inflammatory response. Sepsis-associated encephalopathy is a severe disease that frequently occurs in children, resulting in high morbidity and mortality. OBJECTIVES: In the present study, we aimed to investigate the neuroprotective mechanism of ginsenoside Rg1 in response to septic encephalopathy. METHODS: Effects of ginsenoside Rg1 on septic encephalopathy were determined by cell viability, cytotoxicity, ROS responses, apoptosis assays, and histological examination of the brain. Inflammatory activities were evaluated by expression levels of IL-1beta, IL-6, IL-10, TNF-alpha, and MCP-1 using qPCR and ELISA. Activities of signaling pathways in inflammation were estimated by the production of p-Erk1/2/Erk1/2, p-JNK/JNK, p-p38/p38, p-p65/p65, and p-IkBalpha/IkBalpha using western blot. RESULTS: LPS simulation resulted in a significant increase in cytotoxicity, ROS responses, and apoptosis and a significant decrease in cell viability in CTX TNA2 cells, as well as brain damage in rats. Moreover, the production of IL-1beta, IL-6, IL-10, TNF-alpha, and MCP-1 was reported to be significantly stimulated in CTX TNA2 cells and the brain, confirming the establishment of in vitro and in vivo models of septic encephalopathy. The damage and inflammatory responses induced by LPS were significantly decreased by treatment with Rg1. Western blot analyses indicated that Rg1 significantly decreased the production of p-Erk1/2/Erk1/2, p-JNK/JNK, p-p38/p38, p-p65/p65, and p- IkBalpha/IkBalpha in LPS-induced CTX TNA2 cells and brain. CONCLUSION: These findings suggested that Rg1 inhibited the activation of NF-kappaB and MAPK signaling pathways, which activate the production of proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines. The findings of this study suggested that ginsenoside Rg1 is a candidate treatment for septic encephalopathy.
abstract_zh: 背景：脓毒症常发生于感染后患者，与死亡高度相关。脓毒性脑病以中枢神经系统功能障碍为特征，其根本原因是全身性炎症反应。脓毒症相关性脑病是一种常见于儿童的严重疾病，导致高发病率和死亡率。目的：本研究旨在探讨人参皂苷Rg1对脓毒性脑病的神经保护机制。方法：通过细胞活力、细胞毒性、ROS反应、凋亡检测及脑组织学检查，评估人参皂苷Rg1对脓毒性脑病的影响。通过qPCR和ELISA检测IL-1β、IL-6、IL-10、TNF-α和MCP-1的表达水平，评估炎症活性。通过western blot检测p-Erk1/2/Erk1/2、p-JNK/JNK、p-p38/p38、p-p65/p65和p-IκBα/IκBα的产生，评估炎症信号通路活性。结果：LPS刺激导致CTX TNA2细胞中细胞毒性、ROS反应和凋亡显著增加，细胞活力显著降低，并引起大鼠脑损伤。此外，IL-1β、IL-6、IL-10、TNF-α和MCP-1的产生在CTX TNA2细胞和脑中显著受到刺激，证实了脓毒性脑病体外和体内模型的建立。Rg1处理显著降低了LPS诱导的损伤和炎症反应。Western blot分析表明，Rg1显著降低了LPS诱导的CTX TNA2细胞和脑中p-Erk1/2/Erk1/2、p-JNK/JNK、p-p38/p38、p-p65/p65和p-IκBα/IκBα的产生。结论：这些发现表明，Rg1抑制了NF-κB和MAPK信号通路的激活，这些通路激活促炎细胞因子和趋化因子的产生。本研究结果表明，人参皂苷Rg1是脓毒性脑病的候选治疗药物。
